input: Find a local woodturning club to observe

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the user's location or region is essential to finding clubs that are actually nearby — without it, no useful search can be done.
It matters whether the user wants to observe just once as a casual visitor or attend multiple sessions, as this affects what kind of club arrangement to look for.
The user's experience level (complete beginner vs. some woodworking background) affects which type of club environment would be the best fit to observe.
The user may have availability limited to certain days or times, which would narrow down which clubs are actually accessible to them.
Knowing whether the user has transportation or a maximum travel distance helps filter clubs to only those they can realistically reach.
Understanding what the user hopes to get from observing — deciding if they want to start the hobby, find a mentor, see specific techniques — shapes what a successful club visit looks like.
Some clubs are formal guild-style organisations; others are casual community groups. The user's preference for atmosphere affects which type to prioritise.
